facts.subject: Eric Clapton's 'Layla' (Derek and the Dominos, album 'Layla and Other Assorted Love Songs', 1970) was inspired by Nizami Ganjavi's 'Layla and Majnun' (Wikipedia 'Layla (song)', 'Nizami Ganjavi', 'Layla and Majnun'; Leiden University 2019 'Nezami wrote Layla and Majnun as early as 1188'; Far Out Magazine; Azerbaijan International 6.3 (1998) 'Eric Clapton Song Inspired by Nizami, 12th century Azerbaijani Poet'). Clapton got the story/book from his friend Ian Dallas (later Abdalqadir as-Sufi) (Wikipedia Layla (song), both namings). It mirrored his love for Pattie Boyd, then wife of George Harrison; Clapton and Boyd later married (Wikipedia). Layla and Majnun composed 1188 CE as the 3rd poem of Nizami's Khamsa (Wikipedia Layla and Majnun; Leiden). 1188 → 1970 = 782 years. Rolling Stone 500 Greatest Songs (2004): #27; acoustic (Unplugged) version won the 1993 Grammy for Best Rock Song (Wikipedia Layla (song)). Nizami c. 1141–1209; his birthplace and mausoleum are in Ganja, Azerbaijan (Wikipedia). NOT used: Nizami 'Persian vs Azerbaijani' labels (say 'gəncəli şair'), exact couplet count, mausoleum year.

facts.subject: Baku city population (Presidential Library 'bakucity.preslib.az' table 'Population change in Baku city (thsd. persons)': 1897 112.2; 1920 312.7; 1926 527.2; 1939 791.2; 1959 987.2; 1970 1265.5; 1979 1549.8; 1989 1794.9; 1999 1788.9; 2008 2005.6; 2021 2300.5. Same page: '14.500 people lived in the city in 1863 … In 1897, 111.904'. US Library of Congress Country Study (countrystudies.us) and Wikipedia 'Baku': 'about 13,000 in the 1860s to 112,000 in 1897 and 215,000 in 1913'. Wikipedia Timeline of Baku: 1860 13,381; 1897 112,253. Latest: 2,344,900 (2024, State Statistics Committee via Wikipedia infobox). So: 1860s < 15 000 → 2024 ≈ 2.34 million = more than 150× (2 344 900 / 14 500 ≈ 162; / 13 000 ≈ 180). Oil boom: 1860s → 1897 ≈ 8× in ~35 years. Passed 1 million between 1959 (987.2k) and 1970 (1 265.5k); passed 2 million in 2008 (2 005.6k). 1990s plateau: 1989 1 794.9k → 1999 1 788.9k (flat for 10 years). 1913 figure DISAGREES (215k vs 237k vs 214,672) → not used.
